name: Girona-Costa Brava Airport
before:
The Costa Brava's airport, 12.5 km south west of Girona, and often sold as a Barcelona alternative. Be clear with a client on that: Barcelona city centre is 74 km away.

For the coast it is genuinely well placed. Buses run to Lloret de Mar, Blanes, Tossa de Mar, Calella and the other Maresme resorts, and a second line covers the northern Costa Brava through Figueres, Roses and Calella de Palafrugell. There are also coaches to Andorra and to Perpignan, and the French border is about forty minutes by road, which makes this a sensible arrival for the Pyrenees and Andorran ski resorts.

Into Barcelona the bus takes about 75 minutes and is timed to the flights. Into Girona it is 25 minutes, hourly.

The terminal is a single two storey building with 33 check in desks downstairs and 11 gates above.

The airport was built in 1965 and stayed quiet until the early 2000s, when Ryanair made it one of its European bases and traffic grew sharply.
after:
The Costa Brava's airport, 10 km south west of Girona. It is often sold as a Barcelona alternative, and Ryanair calls it Barcelona Girona, so be clear with a client that Barcelona city centre is more than 70 km away.

For the coast it is well placed: buses run to Lloret de Mar, Tossa de Mar, Blanes and Calella. Coaches also go to Perpignan in France. The bus into Barcelona is timed to the flights, and another line runs into Girona. It is close to the Pyrenees too.

There is one terminal. The airport dates from the 1960s, and traffic grew sharply after budget airlines arrived in 2003. Ryanair lists it as one of its bases.
